cues.en: But first, let me begin by clarifying the purpose of nonviolent communication. Its purpose is to help you to do what you already know how to do. Now, why do we need to learn something today that you already know how to do? Because sometimes we forget to do this. We forget because we've been educated to forget. Now, what is it that I'm talking about that we already know how to do? The purpose of this process is to help us
cues.zh: 首先，我想先澄清一下非暴力沟通的目的。它的目的是帮助你做到你原本就懂得如何去做的事情。既然是你原本就懂得的事，为什么我们今天还要学呢？因为有时候我们会忘记怎么做。我们之所以会忘记，是因为我们所受的教育让我们遗忘了。那么，我所说的大家本来就懂得的事到底是什么呢？这个过程的目的，就是帮助我们

cues.en: to connect in a way that makes natural giving possible. Natural giving possible. What do I mean by natural giving? Let me do you a song to make it clear what I mean by natural giving.
cues.zh: 建立起一种能让“自然给予”成为可能的连结。让自然给予成为可能。我说的“自然给予”是什么意思呢？让我给你们唱首歌，来解释一下什么是自然给予。

cues.en: And you know my giving isn't done to put you in my debt But because I want to live the love I feel for you to receive with grace Maybe the greatest giving is no way that I can separate the two When you give to me, I give you my regret When you take, I feel so given to
cues.zh: 你知道我的给予不是为了让你欠我人情，而是因为我想活出对你的爱；优雅地接受，或许就是最棒的给予；我无法将两者分开；当你给予我时，我也欣然接纳；当你接受时，我感到无比充盈

cues.en: You all know that giving. You know how to do it. And that's what I'm interested in. Remembering to stay with that quality of giving moment by moment in any connection. But we also all know that it's easy to lose it. It's easy to lose that connection so that instead of enjoying that quality of giving, which is possible every moment in every contact we have, in spite of how precious that is, we forget.
cues.zh: 你们都知道这种给予。你们懂得该怎么做。而这也正是我所关心的：在任何连结中，时刻牢记保持这种给予的品质。但我们也都知道，这种感觉很容易遗失。我们很容易失去这种连结，以至于尽管这种给予如此珍贵，尽管在我们彼此接触的每一刻它都唾手可得，我们却没能去享受它，我们把它给忘了。

cues.en: And instead of playing the game that that song is about, which I call Making Life Wonderful. It's the most fun game I've ever heard. Instead, much of the time we play another game called Who's Right? Have you ever played that game? It's a game where everybody loses. Isn't this amazing that we all know about this quality of giving that the song was about? It's possible every moment.
cues.zh: 我们没有去玩那首歌里唱的游戏——我称之为“让生活变得更美好”，这是我听过最有趣的游戏。相反，我们大部分时间都在玩另一个游戏，叫作“谁是对的？”。你们玩过这个游戏吗？那是一个全盘皆输的游戏。难道不令人惊讶吗？我们明明都知道歌里唱的那种给予，它在每一刻都是可能的，

cues.en: We find that the richest thing to do and much of our life we end up playing who's right. Now the game of who's right involves two of the most devious things human beings have ever come upon. One, punishment. See, because if you're wrong in the game of who's right, then you deserve to suffer. Can you imagine a more diabolical concept to educate people?
cues.zh: 我们觉得那是人生最丰盛的事，可我们生命中的大部分时间，却都在玩“谁是对的”。这个“谁是对的”的游戏，包含了人类所发明出的两种最邪恶的手段。第一种，惩罚。你看，因为在“谁是对的”这个游戏里，如果你错了，你就活该受苦。你能想象出比这更毒害人心的教育理念吗？

cues.en: If you haven't already abstained from punishment, I'm sure by the end of the day, that will no longer be a part of your consciousness. No more punishment. You won't do it in your families. We'll get rid of it with criminals. It just makes things more violent. We'll find other ways to deal with other nations besides punishment. No more punishment. No more reward. It's the same game. It's part of the game of who's right. If you're right, then you get rewarded.
cues.zh: 如果你现在还没完全摒弃惩罚，我相信到今天结束时，你的意识里将不再有这个概念。不再有惩罚。你不会在家庭中施加惩罚，我们也不会再对罪犯施加惩罚，因为这只会让暴力升级；在处理国家间关系时，我们也会找到除惩罚之外的其他方式。不再有惩罚，也不再有奖励。它们是同一套把戏，都属于“谁是对的”这个游戏。要是你对了，就会得到奖励；

cues.en: Wrong, you get punished. No more. No more. It's created enough violence on the planet. No more guilt induction. No more shame. No more concepts of duty and obligation. Just what the song is about. Natural giving. So how did we get off target? We got off target according to Walter Wink, a theologian.
cues.zh: 要是错了，就会受到惩罚。别再这样了。够了。这给地球带来了太多的暴力。不要再去引发内疚，不要再去制造羞耻，不要再灌输所谓的职责和义务概念。只要那首歌里所唱的：自然给予。那么，我们究竟是怎么偏离轨道的呢？根据神学家 Walter Wink 的说法，我们之所以偏离了轨道，

cues.en: writes in his book, The Powers That Be, we got off target about 5,000 years ago. We got off target because we started to get some wild thinking, wild thinking that human beings are innately evil. And when you believe that, that human beings are innately evil, then the things aren't going as we would like. What's the corrective process? The corrective process is penitence.
cues.zh: Wink 在《The Powers That Be》中写道，大约5000年前我们偏离了正轨。我们偏离正轨，是因为开始有了一些疯狂的念头——认为人天生邪恶。当你相信人天生邪恶，而事情又没有按我们希望的发展时，矫正过程是什么？矫正过程就是忏悔。

cues.en: When people are evil, you think that the way to bring about change when people are behaving in a way you don't like is to make people hate themselves for what they're doing. So for these political reasons and theological reasons, we started to develop a language that I call jackal language. It's a language that cuts us off from life and makes it very easy to be violent. Very easy to be violent. In fact...
cues.zh: 当人们邪恶时，你认为，当别人的行为不合你意，要带来改变的方法，就是让他们为自己的所作所为憎恨自己。所以出于这些政治和神学原因，我们开始发展出一种我称为“豺狗语言”的语言。这种语言把我们与生命切断，让暴力变得非常容易。非常容易。事实上……

cues.en: In that book I mentioned, Wink says that domination cultures, one of the things you have to educate people is to make violence enjoyable. And we've done a good job of that. We make violence enjoyable in our culture. The two hours a night from seven to nine when children are watching television the most, in 75% of the programs they watch, the hero either kills somebody or beats them up.
cues.zh: 在我提到的那本书里，Wink 说，在支配文化中，你必须教育人们的一件事，就是让暴力变得令人愉悦。而我们做得很好。在我们的文化里，我们让暴力变得令人愉悦。晚上七点到九点这两个小时，是孩子们看电视最多的时候；他们看的节目里，75% 的主角要么杀人，要么打人。

cues.en: And when does this happen at the climax of the program? We've been educated for quite a while to make violence enjoyable. So even though I think what that song was about is what is really closer to our nature, this natural giving, we've been educated to make violence enjoyable and educated in a way we can even be violent to our children. So what is jackal language like?
cues.zh: 而这发生在什么时候？在节目的高潮。我们被教育了相当久，要让暴力变得令人愉悦。所以，尽管我认为那首歌所讲的——这种天然的给予——才更接近我们的本性，我们却被教育成让暴力令人愉悦，甚至被教育到可以对自己的孩子施暴。那么，豺狗语言是什么样子？

cues.en: See, Jackal language, as I've mentioned, is a language of moralistic judgments. Think in terms of who's right, who's wrong, who's good, who's bad. And when you mention change, yes, we want change at times. So how do you get change in the Jackal system? Watch a parent try to bring about change in the child. This is a parent teaching a young child, say, one of the most important words in Jackal. Say, you're sorry. I'm thawy.
cues.zh: 你看，正如我提到的，豺狗语言是一种道德评判的语言。用谁对、谁错、谁好、谁坏来思考。说到改变，是的，我们有时想要改变。那么在豺狗体系里，你怎么获得改变？看看一位家长如何试图让孩子改变。这是一位家长在教年幼的孩子说豺狗语言中最重要的词之一。说：“对不起。”孩子说：“对不几。”

cues.en: You're not really sorry. I can see it. You're not really sorry. I'm sorry. Okay, I forgive you. Can you imagine a game like that? Can you imagine a parent responding to a child that way? And if a parent is going to do that to a child in their own family, what are they going to do to people from other cultures who behave in a way they don't appreciate? So of course you're going to have violence wherever you have this kind of thinking. In cultures that do not have this thinking, you don't see violence.
cues.zh: “你不是真的道歉。我看得出来。你不是真的道歉。”“对不起。”“好，我原谅你。”你能想象这样的游戏吗？你能想象一位家长这样回应孩子吗？如果一位家长会对自己家里的孩子这样做，那他们会怎样对待其他文化中那些行为让他们不满的人？所以，只要有这种思维，当然就会有暴力。在没有这种思维的文化里，你看不到暴力。

cues.en: So that's how we got off target even though we could be playing the game make life wonderful each moment We have been educated for quite a while to play another game who's right? So what are the parts of this game of who's right of all? I've just mentioned one of them one part is moralistic judgments learning how to go up to our head and Think basically in terms of right and wrong good and bad normal abnormal
cues.zh: 所以，我们就是这样偏离正轨的；尽管我们本可以玩“让每一刻的生活都美好”这个游戏，我们却被教育了相当久，去玩另一个游戏——“谁对？”那么，这个“谁对”的游戏有哪些组成部分？我刚提到了其中一个。一个部分就是道德评判：学会如何走到我们的头脑里，基本用对错、好坏、正常不正常来思考。

cues.en: I learned this game very well. I speak several dialects of Jackal. I grew up in Detroit. We spoke a rather harsh dialect of Jackal. You might call it Detroit Jackal. For example, if I'm out driving, and someone is driving in a way that I don't like, and again, I want to install change, you see. I roll down the window. Idiot! Now, theoretically, the person is supposed to repent.
cues.zh: 这个游戏我学得很好。我会说好几种豺狗方言。我在底特律长大。我们说的是一种相当刺耳的豺狗方言。你可以叫它“底特律豺狗”。比如，我开车出门，有人开车的方式我不喜欢，而我又想促成改变，你明白。我摇下车窗。“白痴！”按理论，对方应该悔改。

cues.en: I confess I was wrong, sir. I will change the air of my ways. It's a great theory. It didn't work. I've tried it more than once. It doesn't work. So I thought maybe it was that particular dialect of Jackal. So I decided to get the more cultured use of Jackal. So I went to the university and got a doctor's degree in professional Jackal. Now when somebody's driving in a way I don't like, I roll down the window.
cues.zh: 我承认我错了，先生，我会改过自新。理论听着很棒，但根本不管用。我试过不止一次，真的行不通。于是我心想，可能只是那种特定的“豺狗”方言不行。所以我决定去学更有修养的“豺狗”话。于是我去了大学，拿了个专业“豺狗”话的博士学位。现在要是有人开车不合我心意，我就摇下车窗。

cues.en: Psychopath still doesn't work. There's another part of this language of Jackal. That's very important. You see a language that denies choice, denies responsibility for our actions. I use the word amshprah for this part, having read an interview with the Nazi war criminal Adolf Eichmann at his trial for war crimes in Jerusalem.
cues.zh: 骂一句“精神病”——还是不管用。这种“豺狗”语言还有一个很重要的部分。你看，这是一种否定选择、逃避自身行为责任的语言。读过纳粹战犯 Adolf Eichmann 在耶路撒冷受审时的一篇访谈后，我用 Amtssprache 这个词来指代这部分语言。

cues.en: Eichmann was asked, was it hard to send tens of thousands of people to their death? And Eichmann answered candidly, he said, to tell you the truth, it was easy. Our language made it easy. That interview shocked, that answer shocked his interviewer. And his interviewer said, what language? Eichmann said, in fact, my fellow Nazi officers and I, we had our own name for our language. We called it Amt Sprache.
cues.zh: 有人问 Eichmann：把成千上万的人送去送死，心里不难受吗？Eichmann 很坦白地回答说，说实话，挺容易的，我们的语言让这一切变得很容易。这个访谈……这个回答震惊了采访他的人。采访者问：什么语言？Eichmann 说：其实我和我的纳粹军官同僚们，对自己使用的语言有个称呼，我们叫它 Amtssprache。

cues.en: Ampt in German means office, and Sprache language. I'd call that bureaucratic language. He was asked for some examples. Eichmann said, it's a language in which you deny responsibility for your actions. So if somebody asks you why you did it, you say, I had to. Then you don't feel so bad if you have to do it. You see, you're not responsible. But why did you have to, Jack? Superior's orders, company policy.
cues.zh: 德语里 Amt 是办公室的意思，Sprache 是语言。我把它叫做“官僚官腔”。有人让他举几个例子。Eichmann 说：这是一种让你推卸自身行为责任的语言。如果有人问你为什么这么做，你就会说“我不得不做”。既然是“不得不做”，你心里就不会那么难受了。你看，你不用承担责任。但你为什么非做不可呢，Jack？“上级的命令，公司的规定。”

cues.en: They made me do it. I couldn't do it elsewise. Very dangerous language, Amspacher. Very dangerous. We have giraffe schools. I use the word giraffe, you see, as a symbol for nonviolence. We'll see today that the language we're going to study is the language of the heart. And so I use giraffe language for that because giraffes have the largest heart of any land animals.
cues.zh: “是他们逼我干的，我别无选择。”Amtssprache 是一种非常危险的语言，极度危险。我们有长颈鹿学校。你看，我用长颈鹿来象征非暴力。我们今天会发现，我们要学习的语言其实是心灵的语言。所以我用“长颈鹿语言”来代表它，因为在所有陆生动物里，长颈鹿的心脏是最大的。

cues.en: Giraffe requires always being conscious of choice, you see. We never do anything that we don't choose to do. But I was teaching giraffe to a group of parents and teachers in one community, and we have giraffe schools throughout the world. We have five in Israel, four in Palestine, some in Serbia, and so forth. And in giraffe schools, of course, we want to make sure that certainly that the teachers and parents never use Amtsbrach.
cues.zh: 你看，“长颈鹿”要求人时刻意识到选择的存在。我们做任何事，都是出自我们自己的选择。有一次，我正在一个社区里给一群家长和老师讲授长颈鹿语言，我们在世界各地都办有长颈鹿学校。在以色列有五所，巴勒斯坦有四所，塞尔维亚等地方也有。而在长颈鹿学校里，我们当然要确保老师和家长绝不能使用 Amtssprache。

cues.en: one of the most dangerous languages in the world. To teach a child, you have to do something. So I was saying this one time in St. Louis, Missouri to a group of parents and teachers, and a mother got very upset. She said, but there are some things you have to do, whether you like to do it or not. It's our job as parents to teach our children what they have to do. I mean, there's things I do every day that I hate to do, but there just are some things you have to do. I said, could you give me an example? She said, well, easy. There's so many. Let me think.
cues.zh: 教孩子说“你必须做某事”，是世界上最危险的语言之一。有一次在密苏里州的圣路易斯，我正对着一群家长和老师讲这个观点，一位母亲急了。她说：“但有些事情你就是非做不可，不管你喜不喜欢！作为父母，我们的职责就是教孩子知道他们必须做什么。我是说，我每天都做很多我讨厌做的事，但有些事你就是不得不做。”我说：“你能给我举个例子吗？”她说：“这太简单了，多得是。让我想想。”

cues.en: Okay, like when I leave here tonight, I have to go home and cook. I hate to cook. I hate it with a passion, but I've done it every day for 20 years, even when I've been sick. Well, I said, I'll be very happy today to show you another way of thinking, another language that I hope would open up happier possibilities for you. Well, I'm pleased to report she was a rapid giraffe student. She went home that very evening and announced to her family that she no longer wanted to cook.
cues.zh: 好吧，就像今晚我离开这里后，还得回家做饭。我讨厌做饭，讨厌得要命，但20年来我每天都做，哪怕生病也做。于是我说，今天我很高兴能给你们展示另一种思维方式、另一种语言，希望它能为你打开更快乐的可能性。嗯，我很高兴地报告，她学长颈鹿语言学得很快。她当天晚上回家就向家人宣布，她再也不想做饭了。

cues.en: I got some feedback from her family. Feedback came two weeks later when I swung through that city again and was doing an evening workshop. And who shows up? Her two older sons. She had four sons. They came up to the beginning to introduce themselves. And I said, hey, I'm glad you guys came up here. I've been very curious what's going on in your family. Your mother's been calling me regularly, telling me about all the changes she made in her life.
cues.zh: 我收到了她家人的反馈。反馈是两周后我再次经过那座城市、晚上办工作坊时得到的。谁来了？她的两个大儿子。她有四个儿子。开场前他们上来自我介绍。我说，嘿，很高兴你们来。我一直很好奇你们家发生了什么。你们妈妈经常打电话给我，讲她生活里做出的各种改变。

cues.en: since the training and He like what happened that first night when she came home and announced that she no longer wanted to cook The oldest son said to me Marshall. I said to myself. Thank God I Said help me understand that one. He said I said to myself now Maybe she won't complain at every meal You see natural giving what I started the day off with that song Anything we do in life that isn't coming out of that energy we pay for it and everybody else pays for it
cues.zh: 自从培训之后——比如第一晚她回家宣布再也不想做饭时发生了什么。大儿子对我说，马歇尔，我对自己说，谢天谢地。我说，帮我理解一下这句话。他说，我对自己说，也许她不会再每顿饭都抱怨了。你看，自然的给予——我一开始用那首歌开场讲的就是这个。我们在生活中做的任何不是出自这种能量的事，我们都会付出代价，其他人也都会付出代价。

cues.en: Anything we do out of fear of punishment, if we don't, everybody pays for it. Anything we do for a reward, everybody pays for it. Everything we do to make people like us, everybody pays for it. Everything we do out of guilt, shame, duty, obligation, everybody pays for it. That isn't what we were designed for. We were designed to enjoy giving, to give from the heart. Marshall? Yes? I'm over here.
cues.zh: 任何我们出于害怕惩罚而做的事，如果不做，所有人都会付出代价。任何我们为了奖励而做的事，所有人都会付出代价。任何我们为了让人喜欢而做的事，所有人都会付出代价。任何我们出于内疚、羞耻、责任、义务而做的事，所有人都会付出代价。那不是我们被设计来做的。我们被设计来享受给予，发自内心地给予。马歇尔？是？我在这边。

cues.en: My son brought me to one of your seminars, and I met you some 10 years ago in Oakland. Now I'm trying to bring my son back to come here. And he said last night, when I told him I was coming here, he said, well, why don't you go? I have a couple of appointments. Maybe you could teach me something. So I thought I would come to learn something. Maybe I could teach him. But I'd like to teach him, and I don't know how to do that.
cues.zh: 我儿子带我去过你的一场研讨会，大约10年前在奥克兰见过你。现在我想带我儿子回来这里。昨晚我告诉他我要来时，他说，那你去吧？我有几个约。也许你能教我点什么。所以我想我来学点东西，也许我能教他。但我想教他，却不知道怎么教。

cues.en: I like to teach him to at least give me the time of day to communicate with him. He doesn't do that willingly. And when I try to demand it, it becomes worse. Yes. So how do I do that? Well, that'll be a good situation to work on today because I'm going to ask everyone to think of a situation right now where somebody's behaving in a way you don't like. So in this case, it's your son who when you ask him to communicate, he says no.
cues.zh: 我想教他至少愿意抽点时间跟我沟通。他不愿意。当我试图强求时，情况更糟。是的。那我该怎么做？好，这会是今天很适合处理的情形，因为我现在要请每个人想一个情形：有人正以你不喜欢的方式行事。所以在这个例子里，就是你儿子，当你让他沟通时，他说不。

cues.en: The first thing I'll suggest is you can't teach anybody anything. And to have that as an objective is itself to create problems. So let's change the objective. Let's never try to teach anybody anything or to change anybody. If that's your objective, you'll create resistance. So that would be my first suggestion today. Never try to teach anybody anything or to change anybody. Is that clear?
cues.zh: 我想给出的第一个建议是，你无法教会任何人任何东西。把这当成目标，本身就是在制造问题。所以我们换个目标吧。永远不要试图去教导任何人，也不要去改变任何人。如果那是你的目标，你就会招致抗拒。所以这就是我今天的第一个建议。永远不要试图教导任何人，也不要试图改变任何人。清楚了吗？

It just kind of gets angry at me. No, it gets angry. That's maybe accurate, but it's a diagnosis. We don't know whether he's angry. He might be scared that, you know, you're going to miss school. cues.zh: 大约10分钟后，当她按照自己的定义开始冲他大吼时，我才看出区别，懂吧？所以，雷是在催你收拾准备上学时提高了嗓门。“他就是对我发脾气了。”不，“发脾气”也许说得准，但那是一种评判。我们不知道他是不是真的生气了。他也可能是害怕你上学会迟到。听起来可能像是在生气。也许是，也许不是。但“提高嗓门”、“气得冒烟”，

cues.en: That you can see. That's observable. Fifth grader Jesse refuses to do his seat work. Refuses is a diagnosis. It may be an accurate diagnosis, but it doesn't tell me what he does. He just says, no, I don't want to do it. Says, no, I don't want to do it. That's the behavior. My husband doesn't tell me things which will affect me deeply. It's the first Jackal Husband I've ever heard of. This is a new experience for me today.
cues.zh: 这些是你亲眼能看到的。这是可观察到的现象。“五年级的 Jesse 拒绝做课堂作业。”“拒绝”是一种评判。这种评判可能很准确，但它没告诉我他具体做了什么。“他只是说：‘不，我不想做。’”说出“不，我不想做”，这才是具体的行为。“我丈夫从不把那些会深深触动我的事情告诉我。”这是我第一次听说这种“豺狼型丈夫”，今天真是让我大开眼界。

cues.en: A student in my class incessantly talks loud, won't stay seated, or keep his hands to himself. I hear about three judgments in there. Let's go over it slowly, because I hear three diagnoses. Say it again, so we'll hear the three diagnoses. Incessantly talks loud. Loud is your interpretation. Louder than you would like. If you want to say it, put it that way. Louder than I would like. Won't stay seated. Won't is a diagnosis. Doesn't stay in his seat after I've told him to.
cues.zh: “我们班有个学生总是不停地大声说话，坐不住，还管不住自己的手脚。”我从中听出了大概三个评判。我们慢慢剖析一下，因为我听到了三个诊断性评判。你再说一遍，我们来看看是哪三个评判。“总是不停地大声说话。”“大声”是你的主观解读。应该说是“声音大过了你的预期”。真要说的话，得这么表达：“声音比我期望的要大。”“坐不住。”“坐不住”是一种评判。“在我提醒后，他依然不坐在座位上。”

cues.en: He might in the future, we don't know whether he will or not, so that's a diagnosis. Doesn't at the moment, doesn't when I ask him to stay in his seat. And does not keep his hands to himself. And does not keep his hands to himself. Okay, since coming to the introductory presentation on Tuesday night, I've been very aware of hearing evaluations in myself and especially in other people.
cues.zh: 他以后可能会坐好，我们不知道他到底会不会，所以那是个评判。只是“目前没有”，或者“在我要求他坐好时他没坐”。“而且还管不住自己的手脚。”“而且手总乱动。”好的，自从周二晚上参加了入门讲座后，我非常敏锐地察觉到了自己内心、尤其是别人身上的各种评价。

cues.en: And so I started to wonder, you know, are all of those violent communications or would there be a way that some of those are, according to this model, nonviolent? I would say that any evaluation of others that implies wrongness is a tragic expression of an unmet need. Tragic in the sense for two reasons. First, it decreases the likelihood that we will get what we want.
cues.zh: 所以我就开始琢磨，这些全都是暴力沟通吗？还是说按照这种模式，其中有些其实算非暴力沟通？我认为，任何暗示对方有错的评判，都是未被满足的需求的悲剧性表达。之所以说是悲剧，原因有二。首先，它会降低我们得到自己想要的结果的可能性。

cues.en: Even if we don't say it out loud, even if we think it, if we are even thinking that what somebody else does is wrong, it decreases the likelihood that we will get what we want. And second, it increases the likelihood of violence. So what could be more tragic than that, than expressing ourselves in a way that gets in the way of our getting what we want and increases violence. Anything that we want to say that implies wrongness on the part of the other person, I'm suggesting is...
cues.zh: 即使我们不说出口，即使只是在心里想，只要我们认为别人做的事是错的，我们得到自己想要的概率就会降低。第二，这会提高暴力的可能性。还有什么比这更悲惨呢？还有比用阻碍我们得到想要之物、又增加暴力的方式来表达自己更悲惨的吗？我想说，任何我们想说的话，只要暗示对方有错，就是……

cues.en: a tragic suicidal expression of an unmet need. Say the need. Learn a need consciousness, which is what we're going to get to now, you see. That's how we evaluate in nonviolent communication. We evaluate from the heart. We make judgments, but we make need-serving judgments. We judge whether what people are doing is meeting needs or not. We don't moralistically judge the person for what they did.
cues.zh: 一种未满足需要的、悲剧性的自杀式表达。说出需要。学习需要意识，这就是我们接下来要讲的，你看。这就是我们在非暴力沟通中评估的方式。我们从心出发评估。我们会做判断，但做的是服务于需要的判断。我们判断人们正在做的事是否满足需要。我们不会因别人做了什么而对他们做道德评判。

cues.en: We judge whether it's serving life or not, because needs are our direct connection with life. They're the life that's going, needs are the life seeking expression within us. So we evaluate with reference to that. And that requires two kinds of literacy, feelings and needs. So let's be sure that we are all speaking the same language when I use the term feelings and needs. So under B,
cues.zh: 我们判断它是否服务于生命，因为需要是我们与生命的直接连接。需要就是正在流动的生命，是内在于我们、寻求表达的生命。所以我们参照这一点来评估。这需要两种素养：感受和需要。所以我要确认，当我使用“感受”和“需要”这两个词时，我们说的是同一种语言。那么在 B 下面，

cues.en: It says, imagine that you are talking directly to the person and express how you feel when the person acts in the way described above. And use this form. Again, we're talking to the other person. We're telling them now what they did. And we say, when you do this, I feel how. How do you feel when the person does what you wrote down under A? Write that down. When you do this, I feel angry.
cues.zh: 它说，想象你正直接对那个人说话，表达当对方以刚才描述的方式行事时你的感受。并使用这个句式。再说一次，我们是在对另一个人说话。我们现在告诉他们做了什么。我们说：当你这样做时，我感到怎样。当对方做了你在 A 下面写下的那件事时，你感觉如何？写下来。当你这样做时，我感到生气。

cues.en: Anger is a feeling created by unnatural thinking. We'll get to that next. When you're not ready to leave at the agreed time, I feel anxious and impatient. When you speak that loud, I feel intimidated. Intimidated is a diagnosis. Be careful of words that are more descriptions of other people than you think they're doing to you, like intimidating you.
cues.zh: 愤怒是由不自然的思维制造出来的一种感受。我们接下来会讲。当你没有在约定时间准备好离开时，我感到焦虑和不耐烦。你说话那么大声时，我感到受威胁。“受威胁”是一种诊断。要小心那些其实更多是在描述别人、而不是描述你以为别人对你做了什么的话，比如“威胁你”。

cues.en: Write down the following as not feeling words. Do not mistake these words as feelings. I feel misunderstood. I feel used. I feel manipulated. I feel judged. I feel criticized. I feel ignored. For example, aren't there times when you think somebody's ignoring you? Don't you feel relieved?
cues.zh: 把下面这些写下来，作为非感受词。不要把以下词误当成感受。我感到被误解。我感到被利用。我感到被操纵。我感到被评判。我感到被批评。我感到被忽视。比如，有时候你觉得别人在忽视你，不是吗？你不也会感到如释重负吗？

cues.en: And at other times, don't you feel angry? You see, so words like that really say very little about what's alive in you. They say much more about how you are interpreting the other person's behavior. And above all, never mistake the word rejected as a feeling. I feel rejected, no. That's not a feeling. That's a suicidal interpretation. Okay, who's got the mic? There's the mic. Hurt, disappointed, disinharmed. Feel angry and betrayed.
cues.zh: 而在另一些时候，你不也会感到生气吗？你看，所以这类词其实很少说明你内在有什么在活着。它们更多说明的是你如何解释另一个人的行为。最重要的是，绝不要把“被拒绝”这个词误当成感受。“我感到被拒绝”，不。那不是感受。那是一种自杀式解释。好，谁拿着麦克风？麦克风在那儿。受伤、失望、灰心。感到生气和被背叛。

cues.en: Angry, yes. Oh, for betrayed. Betrayed is one of those words like intimidated, ignored, misinterpreted, used, manipulated. It's more a diagnosis of the other person than a feeling. What about contracted? Contracted? If you mean tense and like that. Okay, what's that? When you call me up and speaking loudly, tell me you're going to cut off funding. I feel angry and scared.
cues.zh: 愤怒，是的。哦，关于被背叛。“被背叛”就像被恐吓、被忽视、被误解、被利用、被操纵一样。这更多是对对方的评判，而不是一种感受。“紧缩”怎么样？“紧缩”？如果你指的是紧张之类的。好，那这个呢？“当你打电话对我大喊大叫，说要撤资时，我感到愤怒和害怕。”

cues.en: When you leave the dishes in the sink, I feel powerless over my environment and time which feels frustrating and scary. When you start talking loudly in the middle of my sentence, I feel hurt because I think you are not listening to me. The feeling is great, but you're going to lose it when you follow the word feel with the word because I think. Anytime you're thinking, your chance of getting what you need is greatly decreased.
cues.zh: “当你把碗盘留在水槽里，我感到自己无法掌控环境和时间，这让我沮丧又害怕。”“当你在我说到一半时大声打断，我感到受伤，因为我觉得你没在听我说。”感受表达得很好，但一旦你在“感到”后面加上“因为我觉得”，前功尽弃了。只要你一进入“觉得”的评判思维，得到所需回应的几率就会大幅下降。

cues.en: Especially when you follow the word think with the word you then I think you not only won't get heard I predict the defensive aggressive reaction It's going to be hard for people to care about your feelings when you follow that with a diagnosis that implies wrongness So we'll get to that next because we're going to see next that we when after the feelings There's two places we don't go and one is up to our head So we stay in the heart with feelings. We don't go up to the head
cues.zh: 尤其是当你在“觉得”后面加上“你”，比如“我觉得你……”，你不仅不会被倾听，我敢说对方还会产生防卫甚至攻击性的反应。如果你在表达感受后，紧接着进行暗示对方犯错的评判，别人就很难去体恤你的感受。我们接下来会讲到这一点，因为接下来我们会看到，在表达感受之后，有两个地方是我们不该去的，其中一个就是“脑子”。所以我们要留在心里体会感受，不要跑到脑子里去。

cues.en: We stay in the heart and connect with needs, but we'll get to that, yeah. If we want to use nonviolent communication, we want to be sure that we do not use the feeling in a violent way because feelings can either connect us at the heart or they can contribute to more division and violence. So we certainly do not want to ever express our feelings in this way.
cues.zh: 我们留在心里，去联结彼此的需要，不过我们稍后会讲到，是的。如果我们想使用非暴力沟通，就必须确保不会以暴力的方式去利用感受，因为感受既能让我们心心相印，也可能导致更多的分裂与暴力。因此，我们绝对不要以这种方式来表达感受：

cues.en: I feel as I do because you, okay? We never want to express our feelings this way. You make me feel. Now that will be a hard habit to get away from because in a jackal culture feelings are very instrumental to using guilt as a way of manipulating people. The way to manipulate people is if you can convince them that they make you feel as you do then they should feel guilty and change. It's another form of this
cues.zh: “我之所以有这种感受，是因为你……”，明白吗？我们绝不要这样表达感受：“你让我感到……”。要改掉这个习惯可不容易，因为在“豺狗文化”中，感受常被当作工具，用来借由内疚感去操纵他人。操纵别人的方式就是：如果你能让他们相信，是他们让你产生了这种感受，他们就应该感到内疚并做出改变。这是这种暴力游戏的

cues.en: violent game. So, for example, if you are a parent and you want to use feelings in a violent way rather than a connecting way, you would express it this way. It really hurts me when you don't clean up your room, okay? Or you make me angry when you say that. I was talking during the break about one of my happiest days as a parent was when my oldest son went to a jackal school for the first time. He had gone six years to a giraffe school that I had helped create.
cues.zh: 另一种形式。举个例子，如果你是一位家长，想用暴力而非联结的方式利用感受，你就会这样表达：“你不收拾房间，真的很让我伤心”，明白吗？或者“你说那样的话让我很生气”。刚才休息时我还提到，作为父亲我最开心的日子之一，就是我的大儿子第一次去上“豺狗学校”。在此之前，他在我协助创立的“长颈鹿学校”读了六年。

cues.en: But then, I wanted him to learn how to enjoy jackals as well. And in giraffe schools, we also want to be aware that the children are not always going to be in this setting, so we want them to learn how to stay with their own values, regardless of which structure they're in. So he comes back the first day from school, and he looked less than happy. And I said, how's the new school, Rick? And he said, it's OK, Dad.
cues.zh: 但后来，我也想让他学会如何欣赏豺狗。而且在长颈鹿学校里，我们也要意识到，孩子们不会一直待在这种环境里，所以我们想让他们学会坚守自己的价值观，不管身处哪种结构。于是他上学第一天回来，看起来不太高兴。我问，新学校怎么样，Rick？他说，还行，爸。

cues.en: Boy, some of those teachers, dad. I said, what happened? He said, dad, I wasn't even in the front door, really. I was halfway through the front door and some man teacher comes running over and says, my, my, look at the little girl. Can you guess what the teacher was reacting to? Yeah, my son's hair was down to his shoulders. See, in a jackal school, as we all know, authority knows what's right. See, there's a right way to wear your hair as a boy and a wrong way. A right way to do everything and who knows? The teacher.
cues.zh: 天哪，爸，那些老师真是的。我问，发生什么了？他说，爸，我还没进门，真的，我刚走到门口一半，一个男老师就跑过来说，哎呀呀，看看这个小姑娘。你能猜到老师在反应什么吗？对，我儿子的头发长到肩膀。你看，在豺狗学校里，众所周知，权威知道什么是对的。你看，男孩该怎么留头发，有正确方式也有错误方式。做什么都有正确方式，谁知道呢？老师知道。

cues.en: And then what do you do if somebody doesn't do it? You use shame, guilt, and so forth. You use the word girl as though it's an insult. Welcome to Jack-o-lan. So I'm getting burned up, ready to go do a little bat therapy with the teacher. Forgetting all about my teachings. And I said to my son, how did you handle it? He said, I remember, dad, that what you said, that when you're in that kind of environment,
cues.zh: 那如果有人不照做，你会怎么做？你会用羞耻、内疚之类的东西。你把“女孩”这个词当成侮辱。欢迎来到豺狗国。所以我火冒三丈，准备去给那个老师来点“球棒疗法”，完全忘了自己教的东西。我问我儿子，你怎么处理的？他说，爸，我记得你说过，当你处在那种环境里，

cues.en: Never give them the power to make you submit or rebel. So one of the things we want to teach children very early, no matter what structure you're in, never lose track that you are free to choose what you do. Don't allow institutions to determine what you do. I said, hey man, that you remembered that, that's a big gift. I really love that you could remember that under those conditions. Then what'd you do? I put on my giraffe ears, dad, tried to hear what he was feeling and needing.
cues.zh: 永远不要给他们力量，让你要么屈服，要么反抗。所以我们想很早就教孩子的一件事是，不管你处在什么结构里，永远别忘了，你有自由选择自己做什么。别让机构决定你做什么。我说，嘿，小伙子，你能记住这一点，这是份大礼。我真的很高兴你在那种情况下还能记得。那你后来做了什么？我戴上我的长颈鹿耳朵，爸，试着听他有什么感受和需要。

cues.en: I said, you remembered to do that? What did you hear? Pretty obvious, Dad. Looked irritated, wanted me to cut my hair. Hey, wow, man, I'm really glad you could remember that. How did that leave you feeling? He said, Dad, I felt sad for the man. He was bald and seemed to have a problem about hair. So we want children, the same thing we want to teach adults. Institutions can't make you do anything. Other people can't make you do anything. No human being has ever done anything they didn't choose to do.
cues.zh: 我说，你记得这么做？你听到了什么？挺明显的，爸。他看起来很恼火，想让我剪头发。嘿，哇，小伙子，我真高兴你能记得。那让你感觉怎么样？他说，爸，我为那个人感到难过。他秃头，好像对头发这件事有疙瘩。所以我们想对孩子做的，也正是想教成年人的。机构不能强迫你做任何事。别人也不能强迫你做任何事。没有人做过任何不是自己选择去做的事。

cues.en: A Palestinian in the village of Hebron disagreed with me one time. He said, I don't agree with you, Marshal, that we only choose to do. Where was my choice two days ago? A soldier puts a gun at my head and says, take off your clothes or I'll shoot you. Where was my choice? He said, it seems pretty obvious to me. You had a choice of whether to take off your clothes or not. He laughed. He said, OK, I got your point. I chose not to take off my clothes. I chose that soldier knew I didn't have a gun. He was doing this to dishonor me.
cues.zh: 希伯伦村的一位巴勒斯坦人有一次不同意我的说法。他说，Marshal，我不同意你说的，我们做什么都只是选择。两天前我的选择在哪里？一个士兵把枪顶在我头上说，脱掉衣服，不然我就开枪。我的选择在哪里？我说，这在我看来很明显。你当时可以选择脱，也可以选择不脱。他笑了。他说，好吧，我明白你的意思了。我选择不脱衣服。我选择不脱。那个士兵知道我没有枪，他这么做是为了羞辱我。

cues.en: I chose to risk my life to protect my honor. Okay, so I'm not saying we always like the choices we have, but nobody can make us do anything we don't choose to do. So I said, apparently the soldier also chose not to shoot you, or else he was a very poor shot. My children taught me this about nobody does anything they don't choose to do. From the time they were two years old, they educated me that I couldn't make them do anything. All I could do is make them wish they had.
cues.zh: 我选择冒着生命危险来捍卫我的荣誉。好吧，我并不是说我们总是喜欢自己所拥有的选择，但没有人能强迫我们做任何我们没选择去做的事。所以我说，显然那个士兵也选择不向你开枪，否则他枪法就太烂了。我的孩子们教会了我这点：没人会做他们没选择去做的事。从他们两岁起，他们就教育我，我没法强迫他们做任何事。我唯一能做的，就是让他们后悔没那么做。

cues.en: And then they taught me another lesson that any time I would do that, they would make me wish I hadn't made them wish they had. They taught me that violence creates violence. Okay, the next step then. We do not attribute responsibility for our feelings to the other person. Never say that you make me feel or I feel because you. Instead, we are conscious that the root of feelings are needs. Behind every feeling, there is a need.
cues.zh: 然后他们又给我上了一课：只要我那么做，他们就会让我后悔曾经让他们后悔没那么做。他们教会了我：暴力只会催生暴力。好，那么下一步。我们不会把自身情绪的责任归咎于他人。永远不要说“你让我觉得”或“我觉得怎样是因为你”。相反，我们要意识到情绪的根源是需要。每一种情绪背后，都有一种需要。

cues.en: Now, certain feelings tell us that there is an obstruction in our thinking, that instead of our being directly connected to our needs, we have chosen to go off to jackal land. So what are these feelings that tell us that we're not directly connected to our needs? Anger, depression, guilt, and shame. Those feelings are very valuable. They tell us that at this moment, I'm not directly connected to my needs.
cues.zh: 现在，某些情绪在提醒我们思维出现了障碍，我们没有直接连接到自己的需要，而是选择去了“豺狗之地”。那么，是哪些情绪在提醒我们没有直接连接到自身需要呢？愤怒、抑郁、内疚和羞愧。这些情绪非常有价值。它们提醒我们，在这一刻，我没有直接连接到我的需要。

cues.en: Instead, we are up in our head telling ourselves moralistic judgments about somebody. Anger, we're making moralistic judgments about somebody else. Depression, guilt, and shame, we're playing that game on ourselves. But we're not alive, as I would define being alive, which is connected to our needs. Do you make a distinction between needs and preferences?
cues.zh: 相反，我们陷入了脑海中，在心里对别人进行道德评判。愤怒，是我们对他人进行道德评判。抑郁、内疚和羞愧，则是我们把这套游戏玩到了自己身上。但我们并没有活着，按我对“活着”的定义，也就是与我们的需要相连。你区分需要和偏好吗？

cues.en: Yes, we make a big difference as we'll see when we get to the next step now because needs contain no reference to specific ways of getting the needs met. So a woman gave me a very good example of what happens when you say what you don't want in a workshop. She said, you've really helped me understand what happened recently, Marshall. I said to my husband, I don't want you spending so much time at work. And then I got furious with him when he signed up for a golf tournament.
cues.zh: 而在长颈鹿语言中，明确的请求首先是一种积极的行动。我们要说出自己“想要”什么，而不是“不想要”什么。在一次工作坊中，有位女士给了我一个极好的例子，说明了当你表达“不想要什么”时会发生什么。她说，Marshall，你真的帮我搞懂了最近发生的事。我对丈夫说：“我不想让你花这么多时间在工作上。”结果当他报名参加高尔夫锦标赛时，我快气炸了。

cues.en: A teacher gave me a similar example. She said, just yesterday, Marshall, I said to this young boy, please, I don't want you tapping on your book while I'm talking. So he started to tap on his desk. Saying what we don't want doesn't make clear what we do want. But worse than that, if we frame our objectives in getting rid of something, it leads to violence very often. It makes violence seem attractive when we try to get rid of something.
cues.zh: 一位老师也给过我类似的例子。她说，就在昨天，Marshall，我对那个小男孩说：“拜托，我讲话时别敲你的书了。”于是他就开始敲桌子。只说我们不想要什么，并不能把我们真正想要什么表达清楚。更糟糕的是，如果我们把目标设定为“消灭某种东西”，往往会导致暴力。当我们试图消灭什么的时候，暴力就会显得很有吸引力。

cues.en: For example, I was working with some teachers in a school in Rockford, Illinois. Their observable behavior they wanted to work on is, on the average, every three months, 38 broken windows in the school. So we got down to the request. I said, what do you want? Different from the students. It's obvious. We don't want them breaking windows. So you're saying you don't want the children breaking windows? Yes. What should we do? Kill them. Research has demonstrated dead children break no windows.
cues.zh: 比如，我曾和伊利诺伊州 Rockford 的一所学校的老师们合作。他们想解决的可观察行为是：学校里平均每三个月会有 38 扇窗户被打破。于是我们谈到了请求这一步。我问：“你们希望学生做出什么改变？”“这很明显啊，我们不想让他们砸窗户。”“所以你们的意思是，不想让孩子们砸窗户？”“对啊，我们该怎么做？”“杀了他们呗。研究表明，死掉的孩子不会砸窗户。”

cues.en: Almost any time we think of what we want to get rid of it makes violence look attractive and as stupid as that example was I just gave you look in the newspaper on any given day and see how many world leaders are saying we're gonna teach them not to we're gonna get them to stop and they think Violence is going to see this always makes violence seem attractive It's only as I said earlier when we get two questions clear What do we want people to do and what do we want their reasons to be for doing it? Then I think we'll see violence never works
cues.zh: 几乎每次我们一心想除掉某些东西时，暴力就会显得很有吸引力；尽管我刚才举的例子听起来很蠢，但你随便翻翻哪天的报纸，就能看到有多少世界领导人在说“我们要给他们点教训”、“我们要让他们停手”，他们总觉得暴力行得通——这种想法总是让暴力看起来很有吸引力；正如我之前所说，只有当我们想清楚两个问题：我们想让别人做什么？以及我们希望他们出于什么原因去做？那时我想我们才会明白，暴力永远行不通。

cues.en: Okay, so we want to say what we want to say in the positive. What do we want the other person to do? What do we want them to start doing differently? And second, that it needs to be clear action language. We can't do what this one wife did with her husband who came to a workshop with him. She said, I want you to listen to me when I talk. He said, I do listen. No, you don't. Yes, I do. No, you don't. They told me they'd had this same conversation for 11 years.
cues.zh: 好，所以我们要用正向的方式来表达：我们希望对方做什么？我们希望他们开始做出哪些改变？其次，必须使用明确的行动语言；我们不能像那位和丈夫一起来参加工作坊的妻子那样，她说：“我说话的时候，我想让你听我说。”丈夫说：“我在听啊。”“不，你没听。”“我真听了。”“你就是没听。”他们告诉我，这通对话他们已经重复了11年。

cues.en: The problem is with the word listen. We can use the word listen as a need. I have a need to be listened to. But when we move to request, we need to speak action language. What specific action do we want this person to take? We can't use the verb to be. I want you to be more friendly, not doable. We can't use feeling language. I want you to feel confidence in yourself. That's not doable.
cues.zh: 问题就出在“听”这个词上；我们可以把“倾听”当成一种需要：“我有被倾听的需要”；但当我们提出请求时，就需要使用行动语言；我们究竟希望对方采取什么具体行动？我们不能用“成为……”这类动词：“我想让你更友善一点”，这是无法执行的；我们也不能用情绪化的语言：“我想让你对自己有信心”，这也是无法执行的。

cues.en: So we need to be able to make very concrete requests. Try it out with what is under D there. In relation to what the other person did and your feelings and needs in relation to the action, imagine you're talking directly to the person and express a request using this form. I would like you to. What do you want the person to do to meet your needs? I want you to obey my instructions.
cues.zh: 因此，我们必须能够提出非常具体的请求；试着根据D项下的内容练习一下：结合对方的所作所为，以及你针对该行为的感受和需要，想象你正在直接对那个人说话，并用这种句式表达请求：“我希望你……”，为了满足你的需要，你希望对方做什么？“我希望你服从我的指示。”

cues.en: Let's use the word. I want you to do what I told you to do I want you to do what I told you to do and if you were a giraffe You would give that to the person with a little card that said but Please do as I requested only If you can do so With the joy of a little child feeding a hungry duck, please do not do as I request
cues.zh: 我们换个说法：“我希望你照我说的去做”；“我希望你照我说的去做”，如果你是一只长颈鹿，你递给对方这句话的同时还会附上一张小卡片，上面写着：“但是，请仅在一种情况下照我的请求去做：那就是当你能像小孩喂饥饿的小鸭那样满心欢喜时；请不要照我的请求去做——

cues.en: If there is any fear of punishment motivating you, please do not do, as I request, a hopeful reward or that I will like you if you do. Please do not do, as I request, out of guilt, shame, duty, obligation. Life is too short to do anything for anybody out of that. So what I'm getting at is when we do make a request, we want it to be sure that the person trusts that's a request and not a demand. So we'll come back to that.
cues.zh: 如果是出于对惩罚的恐惧；如果是为了渴望得到奖励，或是觉得这样做我就会喜欢你，请不要照我的请求去做；出于内疚、羞耻、职责或义务，也请不要照我的请求去做；人生苦短，绝不能出于这些原因去为任何人做任何事；所以我的意思是，当我们提出请求时，一定要让对方确信这只是请求，而不是命令；稍后我们还会回到这个话题上。

cues.en: But let's just work on the clarity of the request to begin with. Yes. So what is your request? I would like you to do what was agreed upon. OK. Give me the space to complete my thoughts. Oh. Too vague. Give me the space. Let me complete my thoughts. Let me is not doable. Let me show you what I mean. A woman said to her husband, came to a workshop, I want you to give me the freedom to be myself. She says, I do. No, you don't. I said, hold it, hold it. Give me the freedom is not doable.
cues.zh: 但我们先来把请求表达清楚。好的。那你的请求是什么？我希望你能按之前说好的做。好的。给我空间让我把想法说完。噢。太模糊了。给我空间。让我把想法说完。“让我”是没法具体操作的。我举个例子给你们看。一位来参加工作坊的女士对她丈夫说，我希望你能给我做自己的自由。丈夫说，我给了啊。妻子说，不，你没有。我说，等等，等等。“给我自由”是没法具体操作的。

cues.en: Let me? No, that's not doable. Allow me? That's not doable. What do you want from him when you say, give you the freedom to be yourself? It's embarrassing, yes? Say it. Oh, it's embarrassing. Say it out loud. What do you want when you say all of that? I want him to smile and say it's okay no matter what I do. Okay, now you're honest. You see, so what do you want? I want to express myself. Yes, you can do that. Nobody can stop you from expressing yourself. Oh, I'm getting interrupted.
cues.zh: “让我”？不行，那没法具体操作。“允许我”？也没法操作。当你说“给你做自己的自由”时，你到底想要他做什么？觉得难为情，是吧？说出来吧。噢，太难为情了。大声说出来。你说那些话时到底想要什么？我希望不管我做什么，他都能微笑着说没关系。好，现在你坦白了。你看，那你到底想要什么？我想表达自己。可以啊，这你能做到。没人能阻止你表达自己。噢，我总是被打断。

cues.en: You want the other person to wait until you finish speaking? Yes. Before starting? Yes. Okay, that's the doable action. So how do we know? You can only tell whether it's a request or a demand by how I treat you if you don't do it. That's what tells people whether we are making requests or demands. What is their memory of how we act when we don't get what we want? If people have in their memory any punishment on our part in the past when they don't do what we want? Any blame?
cues.zh: 你是希望对方等你把话说完？是的。等你说完再开口？是的。好，这才是可操作的行动。那我们要怎么分辨呢？只有看如果你没照做、我怎么对待你，你才能看出这到底是个请求还是命令。正是这一点让人们明白我们提出的是请求还是命令。在他们的记忆里，当我们没得到想要的结果时，我们是怎么表现的？如果人们记忆中，在他们没顺从我们时，我们曾经惩罚过他们？或者责备过他们？

cues.en: It will now be hard for them to trust that we are making a request and not a demand. It will take the joy out of giving to us. So let's follow that example a little bit more for me to show you what I mean. So I say to you, I'm really lonely this evening and would have a need for some company. Would you be willing to spend the evening with me? And you say, Marshall, I am really preoccupied with some things at work and would really need some space to myself this evening. Could you find someone else to be with you this evening?
cues.zh: 那他们现在就很难相信我们提出的是请求而不是命令了。这会让给予我们这件事变得毫无快乐可言。我们继续顺着这个例子往下看，我来给你们展示是什么意思。比如我对你说，我今晚真的很孤单，很需要有人陪。你愿意今晚陪陪我吗？然后你说，Marshall，我手头工作的事真的很忙，今晚真的需要留点私人空间。今晚你能找别人陪陪你吗？

cues.en: And here's my reaction. Two days later, you, what's the matter? Nothing? You, come on, what's the matter? You knew how lonely I was, if you loved me. Now is it a request or a demand? See, so we can't tell from how nicely it's asked. We need to see how the person treats us when we don't do what they want. That's when we trust that they make requests or not demand. So we are going to pay.
cues.zh: 接着这是我的反应。两天后，你说，你怎么了？我回，没事啊。你说，别这样，到底怎么了？你明知道我有多孤单，要是你爱我的话。现在看来，这是请求还是命令？你看，所以我们不能只看问得多客气。我们得看当我们没照做时，对方是怎么对待我们的。只有在那时，我们才能确信他们提出的是请求而非命令。所以我们总要付出代价。

cues.en: For every time in the past when we used any coercive means to get what we wanted So now at least we don't want to pay for it at anymore. We want to be sure That whenever we make a request it is a request now that doesn't mean the other person will trust it even if it is because unfortunately There's been so much coercion in our world that even if we are making a sincere request The other person might hear a demand. I was working in one school system with a group of students at the school district
cues.zh: 为过去每一次靠强迫手段来达到目的买单。所以现在我们至少不想再为此买单了。我们想要确信，每当我们提出请求时，它确实是个请求。当然这并不意味着对方一定会相信，即便它真的是请求，因为不幸的是，这个世界上存在太多的强迫，以至于即使我们提出的是真诚的请求，对方听起来也可能觉得是命令。我曾在某个学区工作，接触过一群被学区

cues.en: labeled as socially and emotionally maladjusted. Now, from what you've learned today, was that a jackal school system or a giraffe school system? Yes. It sounds like in your example that the person was really disappointed or really let down. Not let down, that's a diagnosis. Okay. They're really disappointed. Disappointed. Really hurt. Okay. So, how could they have expressed that
cues.zh: 贴上“社交与情绪适应不良”标签的学生。那么，从大家今天学到的来看，那是豺狗型学校系统还是长颈鹿型学校系统？是的。听起来在你那个例子里，那个人真的很失望，或者觉得很受打击。不是觉得受打击，那是诊断式的评价。好的。他们真的很失望。失望。真的很受伤。好的。那么，他们该如何表达，

cues.en: without being a demand, but not suppressing their fact that they're really disappointed. They could say, so you have a lot to do right now, and it would really meet your need to be by yourself. Yeah. And the kind of mood I'm in right now, I really trust that you would meet it better than anybody else I know. Is there some way that we could find to get your work done and still meet my need for connection tonight?
cues.zh: 既不变成命令，又不压抑自己真的很失望的事实呢？他们可以说，原来你现在有很多事要做，独处确实很契合你的需求。是的。而以我现在的状态，我真心相信换作别人谁都比不上你更能安慰我。我们能不能想个办法，既能把你的工作做完，又能满足我今晚想与你陪伴交流的需求？

cues.en: That's what we call dogging for our needs. It shows respect for the other person's needs. I'm not trying to use any guilt or manipulation. I'm just trying now to find a way to get everybody's needs met. If the person cannot think of somebody to replace them, it will not be a problem. It will only be a problem if I put on these ears and receive in what they said a rejection. If I hear a rejection, that's the problem.
cues.zh: 这就是我们所说的坚持表达自己的需求。这体现了对对方需求的尊重。我不想用内疚感或操纵手段，我现在只是想找到一种让大家的需求都能得到满足的办法。要是对方想不出能替班的人，这也不成问题。只有当我戴上这副耳朵、把他们的话当成拒绝时，它才会成为问题。如果我听出了拒绝，那才是问题所在。

cues.en: You can say I'm disappointed as long as you don't say you disappoint me and as long as you don't stop after saying I'm disappointed See I'm disappointed That's just another way of saying you disappointed. I'm disappointed We always have to end the feeling at the very end of it is going to be a request So we don't just say I'm disappointed. We'd have to say we have to take responsibility for asking for what we want Given the other person has this other need Okay, what do you want then from them?
cues.zh: 你可以说“我很失望”，只要你没说“你让我失望”，并且说完“我很失望”后没有就此打住。你看，“我很失望”其实只是在换种方式说“你让我失望了”。“我很失望”——表达完感受之后，最后总要提出一个请求。所以我们不能只说“我很失望”。在知道对方有其他需求的情况下，我们必须为提出自己的诉求承担起责任。好，那你想从他们那里得到什么？

cues.en: Well, the Jackal doesn't like that game. They don't like to have to be responsible for what they want. They'd rather say, well, if they love me, if they were any kind of friend, I think it's only fair that they want to control by guilt, shame. So the school district asked me to work with these students that were labeled socially and emotionally maladjusted. Poor school system doesn't realize that labels lead to self-fulfilling prophecies. When you label people that way,
cues.zh: 嗯，豺狗可不喜欢这种游戏。他们不想为自己的诉求承担责任。他们宁愿说：“要是他们爱我，要是他们算个朋友的话，我觉得这很公平啊”，他们想用内疚和羞耻感来控制别人。后来学区请我去辅导一些被贴上“社交与情绪失调”标签的学生。可怜的学校系统并没意识到，贴标签会导致自证预言。当你给别人贴上这种标签时，

cues.en: They're going to behave that way. Come on, be honest. If you are labeled socially and emotionally maladjusted, you're one of those students. Doesn't that give you permission to have fun in school? Labels lead to self-fulfilling prophecy. So I knew it was going to be a rough day just by that label. So when I walk into the classroom, it already starts. Half of the students are hanging out the window screaming obscenities at their friends in a courtyard down below. So I made a request.
cues.zh: 他们就会那样表现。说实话吧，如果你被贴上“社交与情绪失调”的标签，成了那样的学生，这不就等于准许你在学校里胡闹了吗？标签会导致自证预言。所以光看那个标签，我就知道今天会很难熬。当我走进教室时，场面就已经失控了。半数学生正趴在窗外，冲着楼下院子里的朋友大吼脏话。于是我提出了一个请求。

cues.en: Excuse me, I would like you all to come on over and sit down, please. I'd like to tell you who I am, what I'd like to do today. Half the students come over. I wasn't sure the other half had even heard me, so I repeated it. Would you all please come over? Now, everybody comes over, with the exception of two young men. Just my luck, the two that didn't come over, the biggest ones in the classroom. And again, I wasn't too sure they'd heard me, and I was praying it might just be a problem with acoustics, so I said...
cues.zh: 打扰一下，请大家过来坐好。我想做个自我介绍，讲讲今天要做些什么。有一半学生过来了。我不确定另一半听没听到，所以我又重复了一遍。大家能过来坐下吗？这下所有人都过来了，除了两个男生。真倒霉，没过来的那两个人，是全班块头最大的。我还是不太确定他们听见没有，心里还祈祷着可能只是声音效果不好，于是我说……

cues.en: Would one of you two gentlemen tell me please what you heard me say? Yeah, you said we had to come over and sit down. You see the problem? I make a request. He hears a demand. So I said, sir, I have learned to always use sir with people have biceps like he did, especially with a tattoo on top of the bicep. I said, sir, could you tell me how I could have let you know what I was requesting so it wouldn't sound like I was telling you what you had to do? He said, huh?
cues.zh: 两位先生，能请其中一位告诉我，你们刚才听到我说了什么吗？“听到了，你说我们必须过来坐下。”看到问题所在了吗？我提出的是请求，他听到的却是命令。于是我说：“先生”——我早就学会了对这种二头肌发达的人一定要称呼“先生”，特别是二头肌上还有纹身的——我说：“先生，你能告诉我怎样表达我的请求，才不会听起来像是在强迫你去做呢？”他说：“啊？”

cues.en: See, that's a radical paradigm shift for somebody who's been educated under domination conditions, domination structures where authorities claim to know what's right, you have to do it or else, you see. So it's a radical paradigm shift in giraffe schools where people don't make demands, they just make requests. So I realize this is not going to be easy with this gentleman. He's probably carrying with him a lot of traces of being punished when he doesn't do what other people want or blame.
cues.zh: 你看，对于那些在支配体系、支配结构下受过教育的人来说，这是一种彻底的范式转变，在那种环境下，权威声称自己知道什么是对的，你必须照做，否则后果自负，明白吗。所以在长颈鹿学校里，这是一种根本性的范式转变，人们从不强求，只会提出请求。因此我意识到，面对这位先生事情不会那么容易。他身上可能背负着很多阴影，因为过去当他不顺从别人意愿或被指责时，就会受到惩罚。

cues.en: I'm not expecting him to give that up right like that. So I said, sir, how could I let you know that I was requesting something of you without it sounding like I was bossing you around? I don't know. I said, just what's happening between you and me right now is much that I wanted to talk about today. I was wanting to look at a way we could interact where nobody bosses others around.
cues.zh: 我并不指望他能立刻放下这些防备。于是我说，先生，我该如何向你提出请求，才能听起来不像是在对你发号施令呢？他说不知道。我说，其实你我之间此刻所发生的一切，正是今天我想探讨的内容。我一直希望能找到一种互动方式，让谁都不必对别人指手画脚。

cues.en: And I didn't expect life to be so easy. That was all he needed. He trusted at that point that I wasn't trying to tell him what to do. And he came over, and we had a very cooperative day. cues.zh: 因为这是道德评判。在我看来，正向的道德评判和负向的一样具有暴力性。也就是说，它们强化了负面评判的存在。如果我说“你是个善良的人”，就暗指世界上有“不善良的人”。这也暗示了我是那个有资格区分两者的裁判。所以别再用赞美或夸奖了，好吗？别再赞美和夸奖了。尤其是当你想把它们当作一种奖励时。

cues.en: That's the ultimate dehumanization, to use thank you as a reward. To say it for the purpose of trying to reinforce something, to get the person to continue doing it. It's like sending a, you know, what goes on at dog obedience school? Punishment and rewards. Giving a compliment or praise for the purpose of reinforcement is giving the dog something to eat to reinforce it for something. People are not for that treatment. And it destroys the beauty.
cues.zh: 把“谢谢”当作奖励，是对人极大的贬低。为了强化某种行为、为了让对方继续这么做而去说谢谢。这就像送去……你知道训狗学校是怎么运作的吗？奖惩机制。为了强化行为而给予赞美或夸奖，就如同为了强化狗狗的某个动作而给它喂食一样。人不该被这样对待。这也彻底毁掉了

cues.en: of thank you. When people have to wonder, is this being set out of that energy? But it works. What does Jackal? Studies in management indicate that if managers praise and compliment employees daily, production goes up. Studies in school show that if teachers praise and compliment students daily, they work harder. Jackal, take another look at the research. I think you'll see that that only works for a very short time.
cues.zh: “谢谢”的美好。大家就会忍不住琢磨：这句话背后是不是带着这种目的？“但这招管用啊，”豺狗会这么说，“管理学研究表明，如果管理者每天表扬赞美员工，生产力就会提高；学校研究也显示，如果老师每天表扬赞美学生，他们就会更努力。”豺狗们，再去仔细看看那些研究吧。你会发现，那种效果只能维持极短的时间。

cues.en: until people see the manipulation and then it no longer works. And it destroys the beauty of thank you because now you cannot even trust gratitude without wondering whether it's being used as a reinforcement, as a reward. Well, what about if I want to build up the other person's self-esteem? What's wrong with that? So, Jackal, you don't see the irony of that? What? If the other person can only like themself when you compliment them, they have no self-esteem.
cues.zh: 直到人们看穿这种操纵，它就不再起作用了。这也毁了“谢谢”的美好，因为现在你连别人的感激都无法相信，总会怀疑这会不会是一种强化手段、一种奖励。那如果我是想帮对方建立自尊呢？这有什么错？所以说，豺狗，你没看出这有多讽刺吗？什么讽刺？如果对方只有在你夸奖时才能喜欢自己，那他们根本就没有自尊。

cues.en: You've just addicted them to your rewards that they only feel good when you say something about them. They have no self-esteem. Okay, how does a giraffe say thank you or gratitude? First, there's three things that are involved in a giraffe expression of gratitude that give us energy to keep being a giraffe. The first thing in a giraffe expression of gratitude is we bring to this other person's attention concretely what they have done.
cues.zh: 你只是让他们对你的奖励上瘾了，让他们只有在你说他们好话时才自我感觉良好。他们根本没有自尊。那么，长颈鹿会怎样表达感谢或感激呢？首先，长颈鹿式的感恩表达包含三件事，这些能给我们力量，让我们继续做一只长颈鹿。长颈鹿表达感恩的第一件事，是具体地向对方指出他们做了什么，

cues.en: that has made life more wonderful for us. See, that's what we need to do daily. We need to bring our consciousness and attention to the power that each one of us has to make life more wonderful. Each of us is a powerhouse. We have words that have the power to contribute to making people's lives more wonderful. We can touch people in ways.
cues.zh: 让我们的生活变得更加美好。看，这就是我们每天需要做的。我们需要关注并意识到，我们每个人都拥有让生活变得更美好的力量。我们每个人都是一座能量站。我们所说的话，有能力让别人的生活变得更美好。我们可以用各种方式去打动他人，

cues.en: that can make life more wonderful. We can provide services for people. We are powerhouses. The more we remember this, we'll not get caught up in any violent games. Why would we use our energy any way other than to make life wonderful when we remember that we have this power? So that's one thing we got to make clear in our expression of gratitude, specifically what the person did.
cues.zh: 让生活更美好。我们可以为他人提供服务。我们就是能量站。我们越牢记这一点，就越不会卷入任何暴力的游戏中。当我们铭记自己拥有这种力量时，又怎么会把精力用在让生活更美好之外的事情上呢？所以，在表达感激时，我们必须明确的第一点就是：对方具体做了什么，

cues.en: not some vague generality. For example, a woman in Geneva, Switzerland came up to me at the end of a workshop. Here's what she said to me. You're brilliant. I said, it doesn't help. She said, what do you mean? I said, you know, ma'am, I have been called a lot of names in my life. Really, I have. Some positive and some far less than positive. And I can never recall learning anything valuable by somebody telling me what I am.
cues.zh: 而不是泛泛而谈。比如，在瑞士日内瓦，一位女士在工作坊结束后走向我。她是这么对我说的：“你太有才了。”我说：“这对我没什么帮助。”她问：“你什么意思？”我说：“女士，我这辈子被人贴过很多标签。真的，各种各样。有的很正面，有的则远算不上正面。但在我的记忆中，从来没有人通过告诉我‘我是个什么样的人’，而让我学到任何有价值的东西。”

cues.en: I think there's zero information value in being told what you are. And great danger, you might believe it. And it's just as dangerous to believe that you're smart as that you're stupid. Both of them reduce you to a thing. We're much more than either of those. But I can see in your eyes that you want to express some gratitude. Yes, and I want to receive it. But it doesn't help me to be told what I am. What do you need to hear?
cues.zh: 我认为，别人告诉你你是个什么样的人，这其中的信息价值为零。而且这非常危险，你可能会信以为真。相信自己聪明，和相信自己愚蠢，危险程度是一样的。这两种标签都会把你物化。我们远比这些标签丰富得多。“但我能从你的眼神中看出，你是想表达感激。”“是的，我也很想接受这份感激。但告诉我我是个怎样的人，对我毫无帮助。”“那你需要听什么呢？”

cues.en: What did I do to make life more wonderful for you? Well, you're so intelligent. No doesn't help Doesn't help. What did I do? Oh, I got you. I got you. She opens up her notebook She showed me two things that I had said that she had written down. She put a big star by them See that helps me now. Okay, that helps me to know that somehow my saying those two things Made this person's life more wonderful. So that's the first thing we need to say
cues.zh: “我做了什么，让你的生活变得更美好？”“呃，你太聪明了。”“不，没用，这没用。我到底做了什么？”“噢，我懂了，我懂你的意思了。”她翻开笔记本，指给我看她记下来的两句我说过的话。她还在旁边画了一颗大大的星。看，这下对我有帮助了。好的，这让我明白，我说的这两句话，不知怎地让这个人的生活变得更美好了。所以，这是我们在表达赞赏时

cues.en: in appreciation. We need to bring to the person's attention concretely what they did that made life more wonderful. Second, at the moment we're giving the gratitude to say how we feel at that moment about the person having done that. So I said to this woman, could you tell me how you feel now as a result of my having said those two things? She said hopeful and relieved. Oh, hopeful and relieved. That gives me much more than telling me what I am that I'm brilliant.
cues.zh: 需要说的第一件事。我们需要具体地向对方指出，他们做了什么让生活变得更美好。第二，在表达感激的当下，说出自己此刻对对方做了这件事的感受。所以我问这位女士：“你能告诉我，因为我说了那两句话，你现在感觉如何吗？”她说：“感到充满希望，而且松了一口气。”噢，充满希望、松了一口气。这带给我的，远比告诉我我是个怎样的人、说我很有才，要多得多。

cues.en: just to know that somehow my saying those two things, now this person feels hopeful and relieved. Now when I hear the third thing, I'll be able to really enjoy this gratitude. I said, what need of yours was fulfilled by my saying what I did that leaves you feeling hopeful and relieved? And that's the third thing we need to see in a giraffe gratitude. She said, I have an 18-year-old son. I've never been able to connect with him.
cues.zh: 只是为了知道，不知怎么，我说了那两件事之后，这个人现在感到有希望、也松了口气。那当我听到第三件事时，我才能真正享受这份感激。我问她：我说了什么，满足了你的什么需要，让你感到有希望、松了口气？这就是我们在长颈鹿式感激里要看到的第三件事。她说：我有一个18岁的儿子，我一直没法和他建立联结。

cues.en: It's been very painful that we never can connect, and I have needed some direction to help me connect with him. Those two things you said met my need for some concrete direction." So had she expressed her gratitude in giraffe, she would have said, Marshall, when you said these two things, showed me what the two things were. It leaves me feeling hopeful and relieved. It meets a need of mine to connect with my son in a way that I want. OK?
cues.zh: 这很痛苦，我们一直无法联结，我需要一些方向来帮助我和他联结。你说的那两件事满足了我对具体方向的需要。”所以如果她用长颈鹿式表达感激，她会说：Marshall，当你说这两件事时——并说明是哪两件事——这让我感到有希望、松了口气。它满足了我想要以自己希望的方式和儿子联结的需要。明白吗？

cues.en: That's how we say gratitude in giraffe, those three things. And it's also important how we receive gratitude. Let me show you how a jackal receives gratitude. Jackal, when you offered to give me the ride just now over to where I'm going afterwards, I feel very grateful because I really have a need to spend more time with my family. And if I took the bus, I'd have an hour less time. It's nothing.
cues.zh: 这就是我们用长颈鹿式表达感激的方式：那三件事。我们如何接受感激也很重要。让我给你看看豺狗式如何接受感激。豺狗，当你刚才提出载我去我之后要去的地方时，我非常感激，因为我真的需要多陪陪家人。如果我坐公交，就会少一个小时。这没什么。

cues.en: If you want to terrorize a jackal, express love or appreciation to it. Really, if you really want to scare a jackal, I've never seen anything scare jackal speaking people more than sincere gratitude or love. Why do you get so nervous, jackal, when you hear it? Well, I don't know that I deserved it. See, jackals have this dangerous concept in their head, deserved. It's a very violent concept. See, it implies that you have to deserve
cues.zh: 如果你想吓住一只豺狗，就向它表达爱或欣赏。真的，如果你真想吓唬豺狗，我从没见过有什么比真诚的感激或爱更能吓到说豺狗语言的人。为什么你听到它时这么紧张，豺狗？嗯，我不知道我是否配得上。你看，豺狗脑子里有一个危险的概念：配得上。这是个非常暴力的概念。它意味着你必须配得上

cues.en: appreciation, you do deserve punishment if you behave in a certain way. See, the concept of deserve is a key ingredient in a violent way of life. If you believe in deserve, you think certain things are worth things and you'll set up a very destructive economic system. You'll set up a destructive correctional system. A very dangerous concept. Well, that's not the only reason. Why else do you get so scared when you hear gratitude, Jaco?
cues.zh: 欣赏；如果你以某种方式行事，你就该受惩罚。你看，“应得”这个概念是暴力生活方式的关键成分。如果你相信应得，你就会认为某些人、事就该得到某些东西，并会建立一个极具破坏性的经济体系。你会建立一个破坏性的惩教系统。这是一个非常危险的概念。嗯，这不是唯一原因。你听到感激时为什么还这么害怕，豺狗？

cues.en: What's wrong with being humble? So you want to have a need for humility? Yes. Well, you know, Jackal, there's different kinds of humility. I'm afraid that your kind is a Jackal humility. I think your kind is the kind of gold of my ear the Israeli prime minister was reacting to when she said to one of her politicians, don't be so humble. You're not that great. But the main reason that I believe that gratitude is so scary for many of us to receive
cues.zh: 谦卑有什么问题？所以你是说你有谦卑的需要？是的。嗯，你知道，豺狗，谦卑有很多种。恐怕你那种是豺狗式谦卑。我觉得你那种，就是Golda Meir——那位以色列总理——在回应一位政客时说的那种：别那么谦卑，你没那么了不起。但我认为，感激让很多人如此害怕去接受，其主要原因是

cues.en: is beautifully and poetically written in A Course in Miracles, where they say it's our light, not our darkness, that scares us the most. See, having been educated in this jackal way to hate ourselves, to think there's something wrong with us, it's a big jump to really see what I was saying, that we have enormous power to make life wonderful, and there's nothing we enjoy doing more than exercising that power.
cues.zh: 这一点在《奇迹课程》里写得优美而富有诗意：他们说，最让我们害怕的，是我们的光明，而不是我们的黑暗。你看，我们受过豺狗式教育，去恨自己，去认为我们哪里有问题，所以要真正看见我所说的事——我们有巨大的力量让生活变得美好，而且没有什么比施展这种力量更让我们享受——是一个很大的跨越。

cues.en: That's pretty, unfortunately, a pretty big jump for us to come to, but we can come to it. So that's how we sage gratitude, observation, feeling in need, same literacy, make sure it's coming from the heart to celebrate, and never to praise, compliment, reward. So any last comments or questions before our time runs out? I'm grateful for all your time and attention.
cues.zh: 遗憾的是，这对我们来说跨度相当大，但我们完全可以做到。所以这就是我们表达感恩的方式：观察、感受和需求，用同样的素养，确保它发自内心去庆祝，绝不是为了表扬、称赞或奖励。在时间结束前，大家还有什么想说的或想问的吗？非常感谢大家的时间和专注聆听。
